title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Organizational messages now supports hybrid-joined devices
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents an API for updating the Intune policy setting that this briefing reports as undocumented. The licensing model should describe inclusion in existing qualifying licences, and the Windows policy advice incorrectly treats Disable Cloud Optimized Content as a setting with a Block value.

claims.claim: The printed Intune route reaches the Enable delivery of organizational messages (User) setting.
claims.quote: Under Platform, select Windows 10 and later. Under Profile type, select Settings catalog. Select Create. ... In the Configuration settings page, select + Add settings. ... select Experience ... Enable delivery of organizational messages (User)
claims.fix: Use the full route 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Policies > Create > New Policy > Platform > Windows 10 and later > Profile type > Settings catalog > Create > Configuration settings > Add settings > Settings picker > Browse by category > Experience > Settings name > Enable delivery of organizational messages (User)'. The missing steps are headings, not additional choices. Add the note 'Set Enable delivery of organizational messages (User) to Allow in Configuration settings.'

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the Intune setting that enables organizational-message delivery.
claims.quote: Update the properties of a deviceManagementConfigurationSetting object. ... PATCH /deviceManagement/configurationPolicies/{deviceManagementConfigurationPolicyId}/settings/{deviceManagementConfigurationSettingId} ... settingInstance ... Setting Instance
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api with graph 'PATCH /beta/deviceManagement/configurationPolicies/{deviceManagementConfigurationPolicyId}/settings/{deviceManagementConfigurationSettingId}', citing https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/intune-deviceconfigv2-devicemanagementconfigurationsetting-update?view=graph-rest-beta. Replace the Row 1 absence sentence with 'The Intune beta API updates an existing policy setting through settingInstance; identify the Enable delivery of organizational messages (User) setting in that policy. This general setting-update API requires an active Intune licence and is not a hybrid-specific endpoint.' Add the row note 'Beta API; the request body sets settingInstance.' The main page identifies this as a settings catalog setting, and the reference documents updating the setting itself rather than merely creating its policy.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center route reaches the Organizational Messages Writer role checkbox.
claims.quote: select Manage roles under Roles. ... select Admin center access, and then select Show all by category. ... Other ... select the checkbox next to Organizational Messages Writer and/or Organizational Messages Approver
claims.fix: Use 'Show all > Users > Active users > user > Roles > Manage roles > Admin center access > Show all by category > Other > Organizational Messages Writer'. The omitted Roles step is a heading, so the current route remains navigable.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates a Microsoft Entra role assignment.
claims.quote: Use the Create unifiedRoleAssignment API to assign the role. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.claim: Assigning Microsoft Entra roles requires an administrator with role-assignment permissions.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: Privileged Role Administrator ... Admin consent when using Graph Explorer for Microsoft Graph API

claims.claim: Show all > Reports > Organizational messages > Manage messages reaches the area for stopping or removing messages.
claims.quote: select ... Show all, and then select Reports ... select Organizational messages. ... Manage messages ... Cancel, delete, approve, and copy messages.
claims.fix: Keep the documented route, but make its early stopping point explicit in the note: 'This route opens Manage messages, where Cancel stops a message and Delete removes it; it does not give the individual message action steps.' The cited page lists the actions without providing a complete cancellation procedure.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no organizational-message cancellation API at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: organizational messages cancel message Microsoft Graph API; "organizational messages" "cancel" "API" "Intune"; "organizational messages" "cancel" "PowerShell". Read main page and FAQ; results document UI cancellation or unrelated calendar operations.

claims.claim: Learn documents no separate administrative switch for hybrid-joined organizational-message delivery.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "hybrid" "switch"; organizational messages hybrid joined devices default enable configuration licensing unmanaged. Read main page, FAQ and Experience CSP; they give a general Windows delivery setting, not a hybrid-specific switch.

claims.claim: The documented entitlement is a mixed licensing model rather than inclusion in qualifying existing product licences.
claims.quote: Page field: model: mixed. Learn: Admins and users can access these advanced features for organizational messages when the tenant has at least one of the following licenses: Microsoft 365 E3, or E5 ... Office 365 E3 or Office 365 E5 ... Windows Enterprise E3 or E5.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Keep the named qualifying licences and the existing FAQ qualifications for Windows and Teams custom messages. The schema defines included as part of a licence the product already needs; the cited passages describe entitlement through those licences, not a separate add-on or consumption model. Pre-made availability without those licences does not introduce another purchasing model.

claims.claim: The cited Learn guidance does not explain minimum settings or delivery handling for hybrid-joined devices that are not Intune-managed.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "unmanaged"; organizational messages hybrid joined devices default enable configuration licensing unmanaged. Read main page and FAQ; they give Intune steps and general supported device types, not an unmanaged-hybrid procedure.

claims.claim: The Learn requirements list only names the device types.
claims.quote: Devices - (For Windows) Only Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices are supported.
claims.fix: Replace 'The Learn requirements list only names the device types' with 'The Devices entry in Learn names the supported device types without giving separate hybrid-specific prerequisites.' The full Requirements section also names roles, tenant policies, Windows versions and firewall endpoints.
